clue.text: Concoction associated with bed and board

definitions.text: Concoction associated with bed and board

parts.words: Concoction associated with bed and board
parts.note: a baked pudding that also names a prank bed with sheets folded short, and a dish served at board, i.e. at the table

explanation.surface: Some mixture linked with lodgings, where you get a bed and your meals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bed and board' suggests lodgings; here the dish is linked with a bed (the schoolboy prank of folding a sheet so the sleeper cannot stretch out) and with board, the table it is served at.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruit pie is a cooked concoction, and the same phrase names the folded-sheet prank bed.

clue.text: He arrives and leaves daily

parts.note: leaves here are newspapers, which this lad drops off at each house every morning

explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like the verb 'departs', but it is the noun: the sheets he leaves on the doorstep each day.
explanation.definitionFit: A delivery lad comes round every morning and leaves the day's newspapers.

clue.text: Arithmetic of a tedious telling in the House

parts.note: something tedious drags on and seems long
in Parliament a division is a vote counted by tellers as members file through the lobbies

explanation.surface: A dull count of votes in Parliament reduced to mere sums.
explanation.walkthrough: In the House of Commons a vote is a 'division', counted by MPs called tellers.
explanation.definitionFit: Dividing big numbers step by step on paper is a classic arithmetic method taught at school.

clue.text: Such an orbital point could be, I agree, within: proven limits

indicators.note: within says one set of letters is placed inside the other
the limits of the word proven are its first and last letters
could be suggests the letters of I agree may form something else

explanation.surface: A scientist conceding that a point in an orbit may be demonstrated beyond doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges I AGREE into ERIGEA, which goes 'within' P and N, the first and last letters of 'proven'.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the point in the Moon's orbit nearest Earth, its closest approach.

clue.text: Miss St Clare is up on a tax fiddle

parts.note: Eva St Clare is the child heroine, Little Eva, in Uncle Tom's Cabin

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young woman named St Clare is in court charged with cheating the taxman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns IS into SI in this down clue. 'Miss' reads as a verb or a fault, but it introduces a young lady, Eva.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodging what you owe the Revenue illegally is the classic tax fiddle.

clue.text: A horse new to dry land

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of A horse are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A fresh mount is brought onto solid ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the six letters of A HORSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Going from sea to shore, as a sailor landing does, means heading onto dry land.

clue.text: Lady's man's sound Cockney origin

indicators.note: sound tells us to say the word aloud and enter its sound-alike

parts.note: a true Cockney is born within the sound of Bow bells, so Bow is the Cockney's origin

explanation.surface: A ladies' man whose roots are genuinely in the East End of London.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney (an East Londoner) is traditionally born within earshot of the bells of St Mary-le-Bow; the place name sounds like the French word for a suitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A dandyish suitor or boyfriend is a lady's man.

clue.text: Needlework pictures

parts.note: pictures worked with a needle, but the engraver's needle on a metal plate rather than a sewing needle

explanation.walkthrough: 'Needlework' suggests embroidery, but the needle here is the etcher's point scratching a plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Prints made from plates scored with a sharp point are pictures made by needle.

clue.text: Garment intended, say, for ceremonial purposes

definitions.text: Garment intended, say, for ceremonial purposes

parts.note: a vest is an undergarment

indicators.note: say tells us the word for intended is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: intended means meant

explanation.surface: Clothing designed to be worn on formal occasions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' turns MEANT into its sound-alike MENT; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Robes worn by clergy at services are ceremonial garments.

clue.text: How long the life whose thread Fate ---?

definitions.meaning: the length of one's days, as in a life's duration
the Fates spin the thread of each life; an old past tense of spin fills the gap

explanation.definitionFit: Lifespan measures duration of life; the archaic past tense of spin completes the line about the Fates.

clue.text: Thomas R.A. is winner of a local election

definitions.text: Thomas R.A. is winner of a local election

parts.words: Thomas R.A. is winner of a local election
parts.note: the painter Thomas, a Royal Academician, read as a man who wins a town in a vote

explanation.walkthrough: R.A. means Royal Academician; the painter's surname splits as gains + borough, what a successful candidate does locally.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighteenth-century portraitist Thomas was a founding Royal Academician, the R.A. of the clue.

clue.text: Will Eccles soon be replanned to avoid it?

definitions.text: Will Eccles soon be replanned to avoid it?

indicators.note: replanned says the letters of the words are laid out again in a different order

explanation.surface: A northern town is being redesigned so that it does not become out of date.
explanation.walkthrough: Eccles is a town near Manchester. 'replanned' shuffles ECCLES SOON BE; the whole clue also describes why a town would be redeveloped.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming outdated is what town redevelopment aims to prevent.

clue.text: Force that gives one globe a new shape

indicators.note: new shape says the letters are moulded into a different form

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A physical force able to reshape a sphere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new shape' rearranges I (one) and GLOBE. 'Force' looks like physics but is the verb: compel.
explanation.definitionFit: To compel someone to do something is to oblige them.

clue.text: Supervised love poetry in French'

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
poetry is verse
the French word for in is en

explanation.surface: Someone kept an eye on romantic poems written in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Supervised and watched over are synonyms for being in charge.

clue.text: Call girl, say, to instruct nurses in it?

indicators.note: say tells us the greeting is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a call to a girl, as in a greeting 'Hi, Jean!'

explanation.surface: A call girl hired to give nurses lessons, an absurd picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call girl' is not the profession but calling a girl: 'Hi, Jean!', which 'say' turns into a sound-alike. Nurses are taught cleanliness.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleanliness and sanitary practice is a key subject in nurses' training.

clue.text: Bow painter (stuck in the railings ?)'

definitions.meaning: a painter is a rope; this one moors a boat by its bow
a child with its head caught fast between railings

explanation.definitionFit: A mooring line at the front of a vessel, and humorously a head held fast in railings.

clue.text: Puppet art, classic style, makes money

parts.note: a doll is a puppet or toy figure
ars is the Latin, or classical, word for art

explanation.surface: Puppetry done in a traditional manner turns out profitable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'classic' points to the classics, Latin: ARS means art.
explanation.definitionFit: The US currency unit names money in general.

clue.text: Culprit walking the plank ?

definitions.meaning: the pirate's victim goes off the end of the plank

explanation.definitionFit: A wrongdoer is a culprit; humorously, one going off the end of the plank.

clue.text: Nothing. : progressive about battle

parts.note: re means about or concerning
action is fighting, a battle

explanation.surface: No forward-looking ideas about the fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing progressive' reads as an aside but is the definition: politics opposed to progress.
explanation.definitionFit: Conservative opposition to change is the opposite of progress.

clue.text: Songs for fishermen

parts.note: rounds sung by several voices, and also what anglers hope to land

explanation.walkthrough: Old part-songs are known by a word that also means an angler's haul.
explanation.definitionFit: Rounds sung in parts share their name with the fish landed by anglers.

clue.text: General retrospective look into a new form of cigar

indicators.note: into says the reversed piece goes inside the reshaped letters
new form of says the letters of cigar are rearranged
retrospective means looking back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: An army officer casts a backward glance at an unusual cigar.
explanation.walkthrough: Agricola was the Roman general who governed Britain. 'retrospective' turns LO into OL, which goes 'into' GRICA, the anagram of CIGAR, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnaeus Julius Agricola was the Roman military commander who conquered much of Britain.

clue.text: Head grower's produce ?

parts.note: a gardener who grows heads: bulbs formed in round heads

explanation.walkthrough: 'Head grower' suggests a chief gardener; it is someone who grows vegetables that form heads.
explanation.definitionFit: Bulb vegetables grow as round heads, so they are the produce of a head grower.

clue.text: Half is calculated inclusive, of public revenue

indicators.note: inclusive says the letters sit enclosed inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Half the national income is reckoned to be accounted for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inclusive' holds the letters inside 'halF IS CALculated'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes matters of state finances and the treasury.

clue.text: Open anger if this Christmas gift is broken

parts.note: frank means open or candid
to incense is to anger

explanation.surface: Someone flies into a rage because a Christmas present was smashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is broken' says the gift's name splits into two words, which give the open anger.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the three gifts the Magi brought to the infant Jesus, the first Christmas presents.

clue.text: A capital orchestra too !

parts.note: the London Symphony Orchestra, abbreviated LSO, is the capital's orchestra

explanation.surface: An excited remark that the city has a fine orchestra as well.
explanation.walkthrough: LSO is the London Symphony Orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: Too and as well are synonyms.

clue.text: "Dick the shepherd blows his ---" (L. L. Lost)

parts.note: a line from the winter song at the end of Love's Labour's Lost, where the cold shepherd warms his fingertips

explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's winter song runs 'When icicles hang by the wall, And Dick the shepherd blows his nail'; L. L. Lost is Love's Labour's Lost.
explanation.definitionFit: A shepherd blowing on a fingertip to warm it in frost completes Shakespeare's line.

clue.text: Thrilling sort of account

definitions.meaning: used as a noun: tension, the quality of a thriller
in bookkeeping, a temporary holding account for items not yet allocated

explanation.definitionFit: Tension keeps an audience on edge, and accountants use a holding account by this name.

clue.text: Cloth-worker gives private tuition

parts.note: serge is a hard-wearing woollen cloth
a worker ant is the crossword's usual worker

explanation.surface: A tailor earns extra by giving lessons on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'private tuition' looks like home teaching; it is drilling privates, the army's lowest rank. The definition describes what this NCO does.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-commissioned officer trains and drills army privates.
